title: Unique identifier linking during registration
description: Homeowner provides unique identifiers (email, username, device serial numbers) during account registration and device enrollment, enabling linking of this data across different contexts or systems.
assumptions: Registration requires unique identifiers for account and device identification

title: Quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of account information with enrolled device types and configurations creates quasi-identifiers that could link data to the specific homeowner.
assumptions: Multiple data points are collected during registration that together can identify the homeowner

title: Profiling through device enrollment patterns
description: Home Hub can profile the homeowner based on types, number, and configuration of enrolled cameras/sensors, creating behavioral patterns that link to the individual.
assumptions: Device enrollment data is stored and analyzed by the Home Hub

title: Processing of identified data during registration
description: Homeowner provides identified personal information (name, email, contact details) during account registration that is processed by the system.
assumptions: Registration requires personally identifiable information

title: Unique identifiers stored in Home Hub
description: Home Hub stores unique references to the homeowner's identity (account ID, device IDs) that can be used to identify the data subject.
assumptions: Home Hub maintains persistent storage of registration data

title: Revealing attributes from device enrollment
description: Device types, locations, and configurations enrolled reveal attributes about the homeowner (e.g., security concerns, home layout, lifestyle patterns).
assumptions: Device enrollment includes metadata about device placement and capabilities

title: Attributable registration data
description: Registration records create data that can be used to attribute account creation and device enrollment actions to the specific homeowner, preventing denial of these actions.
assumptions: Registration creates persistent audit trails or logs

title: Metadata impacting deniability
description: Communication metadata during registration (timestamps, IP addresses, device fingerprints) could contain unintended data impacting deniability claims about the registration activity.
assumptions: Registration communication generates metadata that is logged or observable

title: Observed registration communications
description: The registration data flow itself could be observed by network monitors or attackers, revealing that registration is occurring and potentially exposing data in transit.
assumptions: Registration communication traverses network infrastructure that could be monitored

title: Application side effects from registration
description: Registration creates side effects (database entries, configuration changes, notifications) that could be detected and used to infer the homeowner's activities.
assumptions: Registration triggers system changes that leave detectable traces

title: Excessive data type sensitivity
description: Registration may collect more sensitive personal data types than functionally required for basic account and device enrollment.
assumptions: Registration form may request optional or unnecessary personal information
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific registration form design

title: Excessive amount of personal data
description: Registration process may collect an excessive amount of personal data beyond what is needed for account creation and device enrollment.
assumptions: Registration may request more fields than functionally necessary

title: Extended data retention
description: Registration data may be stored longer than functionally needed for account and device management purposes.
assumptions: Home Hub may retain registration data indefinitely without clear retention policy
uncertainty_note: Depends on Home Hub data retention policies

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of all personal data being collected, processed, or stored during registration and device enrollment.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Lack of processing preferences control
description: Homeowner may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their personal data is processed during and after registration.
assumptions: Registration may not provide granular consent options

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Registration may process more personal data than actually needed for account creation and device enrollment, violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Registration collects data beyond functional necessity
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data collection practices

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Registration process may not adequately support data subject rights such as access, rectification, or erasure of personal data.
assumptions: Home Hub may lack mechanisms for data subject rights fulfillment

title: Guest access linked via temporary code
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest can serve as a unique identifier that links the guest to the access event. The Home Hub processes and potentially logs this code, creating a link between the guest and their door access activity.
assumptions: The Home Hub stores or logs access codes and timestamps

title: Access code as identifier
description: The temporary access code functions as a unique reference to the guest's identity or session. When processed by the Home Hub, this code can be used to identify or track the specific guest who accessed the door.
assumptions: The access code is unique per guest/session and can be traced back to the guest

title: Access action attributable to guest
description: The access code entry creates a data record that can be attributed to the guest, preventing them from denying they accessed the door. The Home Hub's processing of this code creates evidence of the guest's action.
assumptions: The Home Hub maintains logs of access code entries

title: Access communication observed
description: The Home Hub can detect and observe the guest's communication (access code entry) when they attempt to unlock the door. This observation reveals the guest's presence and access attempt.
assumptions: The Home Hub processes and records access attempts

title: Sensitive access code data collected
description: The temporary access code is a sensitive data type that should only be collected when strictly required. While necessary for door unlocking, the code's sensitivity requires careful handling to prevent unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Access codes are considered sensitive authentication data

title: Access code retention beyond necessity
description: If the Home Hub retains access codes or access logs longer than functionally needed for door unlocking, this constitutes unnecessary data retention. Temporary codes should be deleted after use or after a short retention period.
assumptions: The Home Hub may store access logs for security or audit purposes

title: Guest unaware of data processing
description: The guest may not be aware that their access code entry is being processed, logged, or stored by the Home Hub. They may not understand what data is collected or how it is used beyond door unlocking.
assumptions: Guests are not informed about data processing practices

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: If the Home Hub collects or retains more data than necessary (e.g., storing access codes longer than needed, logging unnecessary metadata), this could violate the data minimization principle under GDPR.
assumptions: The system may collect or retain data beyond functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual implementation and retention policies

title: Sensitive sensor data collection
description: Motion, door, and sensor events reveal presence/absence patterns and movement within the home, which are highly sensitive personal data types that may exceed what is functionally required.
assumptions: Sensor events contain detailed information about occupant behavior and location within the home

title: Excessive logging frequency
description: Sensor events may be logged more frequently than functionally needed, creating an excessive volume of personal data about occupant movements.
assumptions: The Home Hub logs all sensor events without filtering or aggregation

title: Behavioral profiling through event patterns
description: Stored motion/door/sensor events can be analyzed to profile individual behavior patterns, daily routines, and presence/absence schedules.
assumptions: Event log data is retained and can be analyzed over time

title: Quasi-identifier combinations enable identification
description: Combinations of timestamps, sensor locations, and event types can serve as quasi-identifiers to distinguish and identify specific individuals within the household.
assumptions: Multiple sensors and timestamps create unique patterns per individual

title: Attributable presence evidence
description: Event log records can be used to attribute presence/absence at specific times, preventing individuals from denying their location or activities.
assumptions: Event logs are retained and accessible for review

title: Unawareness of sensor data collection
description: Household members may not be aware that their movements and presence are being continuously logged by the Home Hub.
assumptions: No clear notification or transparency about sensor event logging

title: Lack of data erasure control
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify or erase their sensor event data from the local event log.
assumptions: No user interface or mechanism for data deletion is provided

title: Excessive data retention
description: Sensor event data may be stored in the local event log longer than functionally needed for the system's purpose.
assumptions: No defined retention policy or automatic deletion mechanism

title: Data minimization violation
description: Collection of detailed sensor events may violate data minimization principles by processing more personal data than necessary.
assumptions: All sensor events are logged without purpose limitation

title: Unique identifier linking through device/user metadata
description: Home Hub includes unique identifiers (device ID, user account ID) in video clip metadata during upload, enabling linking of video data across systems and time periods.
assumptions: Video clips contain metadata with unique identifiers that persist through the upload process

title: Profiling individuals through video analysis
description: Cloud video storage may analyze video clips to identify patterns in individual behavior, movements, and activities, enabling profiling of data subjects.
assumptions: Cloud storage system has capability to analyze video content for behavioral patterns

title: Processing of identified data in video content
description: Video clips contain identifiable information such as faces, license plates, and other personal identifiers that are processed and stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: Video clips capture identifiable individuals and objects

title: Revealing attributes in video metadata and content
description: Video files contain revealing attributes including timestamps, location data, and visual content that support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Video metadata includes location and temporal information

title: Video data as attributable evidence
description: Stored video clips can be used as evidence to prevent individuals from denying their presence, actions, or claims about specific events.
assumptions: Video content can be retrieved and used as evidentiary material

title: Detection through observed upload communications
description: The act of uploading video clips to cloud storage can be detected through network monitoring, revealing that video data transfer is occurring.
assumptions: Network traffic can be monitored to detect upload activities

title: Sensitive video data type collection
description: Video clips are highly sensitive personal data containing visual recordings of individuals, which may exceed what is functionally required.
assumptions: Video content captures sensitive personal information

title: Extended video data retention
description: Video clips may be stored in cloud storage longer than functionally necessary, increasing privacy risks over time.
assumptions: Retention policies may not align with data minimization principles

title: Cloud provider access to personal video data
description: Cloud storage provider has access to stored video clips, exposing personal data to a predetermined third party beyond the user's direct control.
assumptions: Cloud storage provider can access stored data for operational purposes

title: Unawareness of video data collection and storage
description: Individuals captured in video clips may be unaware that their personal data is being recorded, uploaded, and stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: People in video range may not have explicit notice of recording

title: Lack of control over video data erasure
description: Data subjects may lack mechanisms to request deletion or rectification of their video data stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: Cloud storage may not provide adequate data subject rights mechanisms

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing all recorded video clips may process more personal data than is actually needed for the system's functional purpose.
assumptions: Not all video content is necessary for system functionality

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video data may be retained in cloud storage longer than necessary for the purposes for which it was collected.
assumptions: Retention periods may not be clearly defined or limited

title: Sensitive motion data collected
description: Motion alert data reveals presence/absence patterns and home occupancy, which is sensitive personal data that may exceed what is functionally required for basic alert functionality.
assumptions: Motion data can reveal when occupants are home, their routines, and daily patterns

title: High frequency data transmission
description: Real-time motion alerts are transmitted with high frequency, potentially more often than functionally necessary for the intended alert purpose.
assumptions: Real-time implies continuous or near-continuous monitoring and transmission

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: Motion alerts likely contain device or user identifiers that enable linking of data across the Home Hub and Mobile App Backend systems.
assumptions: Alerts include identifiers to route to correct user account

title: Identifier in transit
description: The data flow contains unique references to the identity of the data subject (device/user ID) that could be intercepted or logged.
assumptions: Motion alerts include user/device identification for routing

title: Observed communications reveal monitoring
description: The communication itself reveals that motion monitoring is active, which could be detected by network observers.
assumptions: Network traffic patterns could indicate motion detection system activity

title: Profiling through motion patterns
description: The Mobile App Backend can analyze motion alert patterns to profile individual behavior, routines, and presence patterns over time.
assumptions: Backend stores and analyzes motion data over time

title: Extended retention of motion data
description: Motion alerts may be stored longer than functionally needed for the alert purpose, creating unnecessary privacy risk.
assumptions: Backend may retain historical motion data for analytics or other purposes

title: Lack of user control over motion data
description: Users may lack control over how motion data is processed, including preferences for collection frequency, retention, and usage.
assumptions: User settings may not provide granular control over motion data processing

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: Processing real-time motion data may violate GDPR data minimization principle if more data is collected than necessary for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Real-time motion data collection may exceed functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific purpose specification and necessity assessment

title: Profiling through motion detection patterns
description: Motion detection notifications can be analyzed to profile the homeowner's behavior patterns, including when they are home, movement patterns within the property, and daily routines.
assumptions: The backend processes and sends motion detection data that could be aggregated over time

title: Processing of identified homeowner data
description: The mobile app backend processes and sends notifications to a specifically identified homeowner, requiring their identity to be known and processed.
assumptions: The system must identify which homeowner to send notifications to

title: Identifier in notification data
description: The notification likely contains unique identifiers (user ID, device ID, account ID) to route the motion alert to the correct homeowner's phone.
assumptions: Notifications require routing identifiers to reach the correct recipient

title: Detection through observed communications
description: The transmission of motion detection notifications reveals that motion was detected at the homeowner's property, which could be observed by network monitoring or interception.
assumptions: The data flow could be monitored or intercepted

title: Sensitive motion detection data disclosure
description: Motion detection data reveals occupancy and movement patterns, which are sensitive personal data types that disclose when the homeowner is present or absent from their property.
assumptions: Motion detection data is considered sensitive personal data

title: Implicit disclosure of occupancy status
description: Motion detection notifications implicitly disclose whether the homeowner is home or away, which is personal data collected as a side-effect of the explicit motion detection functionality.
assumptions: Motion detection inherently reveals occupancy information

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Homeowners may not be fully aware of how their motion detection data is processed, stored, or what inferences can be drawn from notification patterns.
assumptions: Users may not understand the full implications of motion detection notifications

title: Lack of control over notification preferences
description: Homeowners may lack granular control over what motion detection data triggers notifications, how frequently they are sent, or what information is included.
assumptions: Notification settings may not offer sufficient customization options

title: Personal data shared with external analytics vendor
description: The mobile app backend shares device-usage analytics with an external cloud analytics vendor (EE3). This exposes personal data to a third party that may not be under the same privacy controls as the original system.
assumptions: Device-usage analytics may contain or enable derivation of personal data about users

title: Granular device-usage data disclosed
description: Even aggregated analytics may contain fine-grained usage patterns that reveal more about individual users than functionally necessary for analytics purposes.
assumptions: Aggregation may not sufficiently anonymize individual usage patterns

title: User profiling through analytics data
description: The cloud analytics vendor can analyze device-usage patterns to profile individual users, linking data to specific individuals through behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Analytics vendor has capability to perform user profiling on received data

title: Quasi-identifiers in analytics data
description: Device-usage analytics may contain combinations of attributes (usage times, app usage patterns, device characteristics) that serve as quasi-identifiers to identify individual users.
assumptions: Analytics data contains sufficient attribute combinations for re-identification

title: Further processing and enrichment of analytics data
description: The analytics vendor may further treat, analyze, and enrich the received data beyond what is necessary for the original analytics purpose, potentially creating additional privacy risks.
assumptions: Analytics vendors typically perform additional data processing and enrichment

title: Users unaware of analytics data sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with an external cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly disclose third-party analytics sharing

title: Lack of user control over analytics sharing
description: Users may lack the ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their device-usage analytics are processed and shared with the external vendor.
assumptions: App may not provide granular consent controls for analytics sharing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The volume and granularity of analytics data shared with the external vendor may exceed what is actually needed for the analytics purpose, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Analytics data collection may not be strictly limited to functional necessity
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data collection practices and legal basis

title: Highly sensitive video data processed
description: Video clips contain highly sensitive personal data including visual recordings of the homeowner's activities, home interior, and potentially other individuals. This data type is more sensitive than functionally required for simple playback functionality.
assumptions: Video content includes identifiable personal information about the homeowner and their home environment

title: Video content reveals identifying attributes
description: Video clips contain revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject, including visual appearance, activities, home layout, and potentially other individuals present in the footage.
assumptions: Video content is not anonymized and contains visual information that can identify the homeowner

title: Video content enables individual profiling
description: The mobile app backend can analyze video content to profile the homeowner's behavior patterns, daily routines, habits, and lifestyle based on the recorded activities in the video clips.
assumptions: Backend has capability to analyze video content beyond simple playback
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether backend performs content analysis or just retrieves for playback

title: Video data can be used as attributable evidence
description: Video recordings can be used to prevent the homeowner from denying certain claims about their activities, presence, or actions captured in the footage.
assumptions: Video content is stored and can be retrieved as evidence of homeowner activities

title: Lack of control over video data rectification/erasure
description: The homeowner may lack adequate control to rectify incorrect video data or remove personal video data that is no longer relevant, especially if the backend retains copies or metadata.
assumptions: Backend may retain video data or metadata beyond the immediate playback session
uncertainty_note: Depends on backend data retention policies

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing full video clips may involve more personal data than actually needed for the playback functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Full video content is processed when only playback functionality is required
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether video processing is limited to playback or includes additional analysis
